title: Freckle and the Sparkle Drop
markdown:
Freckle the frog lived in a pond that sparkled as if it had been dusted with tiny diamonds. His home was a big soft lily pad, and his very best friend was Pocket, a cuddly grey rabbit plush. Pocket listened so well that even the wobbliest worries felt steadier. Freckle had bright green skin and freckles like little happy secrets on his nose and cheeks. He loved the gentle swish of the water, the tickle of the tall reeds, and Pocket, who smelled of sunshine and clean clothes.

One sunny morning the air shimmered with a special light. The Pond Queen, who lived in the deepest bluest part and wore a crown of dewdrops that twinkled like stars, looked a little worried.

“Oh dear, oh dear,” she sighed, her voice like tiny bells. “My most precious pearl-like raindrop has bounced right off my crown. It has rolled all the way to the edge of the pond, and the sun is getting warm, warm, warm.”

That raindrop held the sparkle for all the other dewdrops. Freckle’s tummy did a little flip-flop, like a tiny acrobat practising. He wanted to help. A fluttery feeling, like a hundred tiny butterflies, started in his throat. He imagined his legs wobbling. His little froggy toes wriggled.

The Pond Queen smiled. “Freckle, Pocket, your lily pad is closest to the edge. Could you help it back to me? It is very light, but it must only be touched by pond water or a friendly dewdrop, nothing dry or rough.”

Freckle looked at Pocket, who gave a reassuring snuggle against his side. “We’ll do it,” Freckle croaked, trying to sound braver than he felt.

They climbed onto their favourite lily pad, which felt wonderfully solid and familiar. With a gentle push from Freckle’s strong legs they glided away from home toward the shimmering edge. The water ahead looked wider than usual. The air felt like a soft new blanket. If the raindrop was not returned quickly, its sparkle would fade, and the pond would lose its shine.

A playful breeze puffed out its cheeks and sent a gust. Freckle’s lily pad wobbled. Pocket held on, floppy ears swaying like little flags. Freckle thought of slipping. He squeezed his eyes shut. His heart went thump-thump. His knees began to tremble. He almost wanted to paddle back to his safe familiar spot.

Then they reached a bigger lily pad, covered in fine velvety green moss. Freckle’s legs felt like jelly. The moss looked slick. It felt cool and damp under his toes, and a faint earthy scent rose from it. What if I lose my footing and the precious raindrop rolls away? Pocket nudged him with a soft paw.

And there it was, resting on a delicate blade of grass near the water’s edge: a single perfect pearl-like raindrop. It gleamed with a soft gentle light, no bigger than Freckle’s thumb, and it felt like the most important thing in the whole pond.

The Pond Queen floated closer, crown sparkling. “Oh, thank you,” she whispered.

Now came the trickiest part. How could he move something so delicate without it shattering or rolling into the dry dust? He looked at Pocket, who gave him a tiny encouraging squeeze. Freckle took a deep breath of air that smelled of lily pads and sunshine. He felt the smooth cool raindrop as he carefully nudged it with his nose.

A little tremor ran through his toes. He looked at his smooth grey luck pebble, the one he always rubbed. He imagined holding it, its familiar coolness. But the sun was still hot, and the raindrop shimmered, so important. With a sigh that felt heavy, he nudged the pebble off the lily pad. It sank with a small splash, leaving a gap where its comfort had been. The water felt suddenly colder.

He nudged the raindrop with his nose. It wobbled, then slipped into the water with a tiny tinkling sound, like a miniature crystal bell. It floated, sparkling, toward the Pond Queen.

With a happy sigh like a gentle ripple, she scooped it up. It settled back onto her crown, and all the other dewdrops gleamed brighter, like a brand-new constellation. Freckle and Pocket watched, hearts light. They turned their lily pad and glided home. The sun was lower now, painting the clouds orange, pink, and gold.

Back on their cozy pad, Freckle snuggled close to Pocket. When a gust tickled the reeds, he felt a tiny echo of the old wobble. This time he noticed how his lily pad bobbed like a little boat, strong and steady. He looked at the sunbeams dancing on the water, and a calm happy smile spread across his face, warm as the sunshine itself.
